minutes.headline: Cable committee approved its FY22 budget presentation for FinCom and sent its town meeting warrant article, subject to town staff review.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee met by Zoom. It approved the prior minutes as amended and heard the manager's report on finances, the Castus streaming fix and the production technician search. It reviewed the Finance Committee presentation page by page and voted to present it next month. It also voted to send in the warrant article after a dispute over its wording.

budget_items.what_was_said: After the month's expenses the retained earnings balance was reported; the manager gave an exact figure when asked.

The town reduced the indirect and fringe charge because no production technician will be hired before FY22. The difference returns to retained earnings, with the transfer executed in March and visible in April.
The position was budgeted as part-time and benefited, with a minimum number of weekly hours. It is already approved and the manager was asked to resume recruiting.

budget_items.what_was_said: The new equipment line was lowered at an earlier meeting because a new studio space is not expected in the next financial year.
The February franchise payment had not been posted. The member wanted the page to show expected annual income from Comcast and added FY22.
A member asked whether the committee will keep paying rent in a new building.
The chair projected the retained earnings at the start of FY22 and said total operations is less than expected income. The presentation relabels the line as expected PAC retained earnings.

budget_items.what_was_said: Pending legislation would put a fee on digital streaming delivery, split between the state, municipalities and community media. It could offset franchise fee losses as viewers move to streaming, but the amounts are unknown.

what_happened.line: The committee voted unanimously by roll call to send its proposed warrant article for annual town meeting, subject to town staff approval of the wording.
It approved its budget presentation, with the changes made, to be presented to the Finance Committee next month; the vote was by roll call, all in favor.
The Finance Committee presentation was reviewed page by page, including the new equipment line, Comcast franchise income and the projected retained earnings.
The manager reported that the town reduced the FY21 indirect and fringe charge because no production technician will be hired before FY22; the difference returns to retained earnings.
A pending state bill would put a fee on digital streaming, shared among the state, municipalities and community media; the amounts are unknown.

why_it_matters: The committee's budget and warrant article go to the Finance Committee and then to town meeting, where residents vote on the town's cable access funding.
Cable access is paid largely from Comcast franchise fees, so a shift of viewers to streaming and any state streaming fee could change that income.
watch_next: The committee's presentation to the Finance Committee next month, and the town staff review of the warrant article wording.
